name: Uniswap
purpose: Automated market maker with concentrated liquidity: LPs provide liquidity inside a price range, traders swap against the pool of one token pair and fee tier.
about: The core is one Factory and one Pool per (token0, token1, fee). A Pool keeps the current price (sqrtPriceX96) and tick in slot0, liquidity per tick, positions per owner and range, and a price oracle. The core never pulls tokens: it sends first and then calls back msg.sender to be paid, checking its own balance afterwards. The periphery (SwapRouter, NonfungiblePositionManager) are the contracts users call; they implement those callbacks, check deadlines and slippage, and pay the pool.

flows.title: Swap
flows.summary: Exact input, one pool: amountIn of tokenIn for at least amountOutMinimum of tokenOut.

steps.say: Approves SwapRouter for tokenIn, then calls exactInputSingle(tokenIn, tokenOut, fee, recipient, deadline, amountIn, amountOutMinimum, sqrtPriceLimitX96).
checkDeadline, then exactInputInternal with the caller recorded as payer in the callback data.
The pool's address comes from CREATE2 (factory, sorted tokens, fee), not from a storage lookup.
Takes the lock in slot0 and swaps step by step until the amount is used or the price limit is reached.
Finds the next initialized tick in the swap direction, within one 256-tick word.
Moves the price toward that tick: amount in, amount out and the LP fee for the step; the protocol's share is split off when the protocol fee is on.
When the price crosses an initialized tick, its net liquidity is added or removed and its fee growth outside flipped.
If the tick changed, writes one observation for this block.
The pool sends tokenOut to the recipient first.
The pool calls back msg.sender (the router) with the amounts owed.
The router checks msg.sender is the canonical pool for tokenIn, tokenOut and fee.
The router pays tokenIn from the payer to the pool (wrapping ETH into WETH when the payer sent ETH).
Back in the pool: requires its tokenIn balance grew by at least the amount owed, emits Swap, releases the lock.
Requires amountOut ≥ amountOutMinimum, otherwise the whole swap reverts.

checks: Integrations: amountOutMinimum and deadline are the user's only protection against price movement; never pass 0 or a far deadline from a contract.
slot0 is the current price and moves with every swap; integrations that need a price should read the time-weighted oracle (observe) or an external feed.
Any contract implementing uniswapV3SwapCallback must verify msg.sender is a canonical pool, or anyone can call it and ask to be paid.
The pool checks its own balance after the callback: tokens that charge a transfer fee or rebase don't behave as the pool expects.

flows.title: Add liquidity
flows.summary: Open a position in a price range and get it as an NFT.

steps.say: Approves NonfungiblePositionManager for both tokens, then calls mint(token0, token1, fee, tickLower, tickUpper, amount0Desired, amount1Desired, amount0Min, amount1Min, recipient, deadline).
checkDeadline, then addLiquidity.
Computes the pool address and the liquidity the desired amounts buy at the current price (slot0).
Under the lock, with the position manager as the position's owner in the pool.
Checks the ticks, updates the position and both ticks, and computes how much of each token the range needs at the current price.
Adds liquidity to the lower and upper tick; a tick that becomes initialized is flipped in the bitmap.
Credits fees earned since the last update and sets the new liquidity.
The pool calls back the manager; it verifies the pool and pays both amounts from the LP.
token0 and token1 move from the LP to the pool.
The pool requires both balances grew as owed and emits Mint.
The manager checks amount0Min / amount1Min, mints the NFT, stores the range and the fee growth snapshot, emits IncreaseLiquidity.

checks: amount0Min / amount1Min protect the LP against the price moving before the transaction; contracts that add liquidity must set them.
In the pool, every position of every NFT is owned by the position manager; the NFT owner is tracked only in the manager.
The mint callback must verify the pool, like the swap callback.

flows.title: Remove and collect
flows.summary: Take liquidity out of a position, then collect the tokens and fees owed.

steps.say: As the NFT owner or an approved operator, calls decreaseLiquidity(tokenId, liquidity, amount0Min, amount1Min, deadline).
isAuthorizedForToken; liquidity must be positive and not more than the position holds.
Removes the liquidity and credits the token amounts to the position's tokensOwed in the pool. Nothing is transferred yet.
Slippage check, then the manager adds the amounts and the fees since the last snapshot to the NFT's tokens owed.
collect(tokenId, recipient, amount0Max, amount1Max); with liquidity left, first pokes the pool with burn(0) to bring fees up to date.
Transfers up to the requested amounts of tokensOwed to the recipient.
token0 and token1 leave the pool.
Emits Collect with the amounts sent.

checks: decreaseLiquidity moves no tokens; anything integrating it must call collect afterwards.
Who can act on a position is the NFT owner or an approved operator; vaults holding NFTs must control approvals.
Fees are derived from fee growth snapshots; review that every path that changes liquidity updates the snapshot first.

flows.title: Create a pool
flows.summary: Deploy the pool for a new pair and fee tier, then set its first price.

steps.say: Calls createPool(tokenA, tokenB, fee) on the factory (the position manager's createAndInitializePoolIfNecessary does the same).
Tokens different and non-zero, sorted into token0 < token1, the fee tier enabled, and no pool yet for this pair and fee.
Writes the parameters, deploys the pool with CREATE2 salt keccak256(token0, token1, fee), deletes the parameters.
Reads factory, tokens, fee and tick spacing from the deployer and stores them as immutables.
The factory records the pool in getPool both ways and emits PoolCreated.
Anyone sets the starting sqrtPriceX96, once (slot0.sqrtPriceX96 must be 0). Initializes the oracle.

checks: The first price is set by whoever calls initialize; integrations must not trust a new pool's price until it has liquidity and history.
Pool addresses are deterministic: code that computes them must use the same init code hash as the deployed factory.
Only the factory owner enables fee tiers and protocol fees; check who that is on each chain.
Callbacks: every uniswapV3*Callback implementation verifies msg.sender is a canonical pool.
Slippage and deadlines on every periphery call made by a contract.
Price: slot0 vs the time-weighted oracle; observation cardinality is small on new pools.
Tokens: fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens break the pool's balance checks.
Rounding directions in SqrtPriceMath always favour the pool.
notes: Mapped: core (factory, deployer, pool and its libraries) and the two main periphery contracts with their callback libraries. Not mapped: Quoter, position descriptor, multicall, migrator, Uniswap v4.
